title: Rapid deploy planning + decision log — week of 2024-11-04
content:
Meeting: Rapid deploy planning + decision log
Week: Mon 2024-11-04 -> Thu 2024-11-07 (notes collected across standups)
Owner: Priya Shah (release-engineering)
Attendees (regular): Priya, Marco, Jordan, Elena, Samir; Ad-hoc: QA on-call (Aisha), SRE duty (Ravi)
Channel: #release-ops (Slack) — thread pinned: rapid-deploy-2024-11-04
Purpose: Triage and schedule hotfixes and small change windows that need expedited rollback/forward decisions. Record decisions, risk assessment, and owners for follow-up. This doc is a single source-of-truth for small emergency and rapid-sprint deploys for the week.

Agenda (running):
- Quick state (canary health, critical alerts)
- Prioritize outstanding hotfix tickets (severity P0/P1)
- Decide deploy windows and rollback signals
- Assign owners and verification tasks (QA, metrics checks)
- Note blockers and escalate items

Summary / Highlights:
- Canary cluster showed intermittent p95 latency spikes between 11/04 02:00-03:30 UTC. Root cause narrowed to KV cache eviction edge-case when sequence lengths > 4k. Impacts: hosted-api text-generation only; embeddings unaffected.
- Two urgent PRs identified for fast-track: runtime connection pooling fix (PR 542) and model-routing fallback change (RLE-1987).
- Decided to schedule a limited canary push to dedicated canary region (eu-west-2) during low-traffic window (2024-11-06 01:00-03:00 UTC) with manual rollback window of 30 minutes.

Observations / Signals (raw notes):
- 11/04 01:55 UTC: Pager alert p95 > 3500ms on canary gen endpoints.
- 11/04 02:10 UTC: Error budget for canary still healthy but transient spike correlated with long-seq requests from internal test harness.
- 11/05 16:20 UTC: QA reproduced KV eviction on local env using instrumented long-seq test (steps in linked PR).
- 11/06 00:45 UTC: Preflight smoke passed in staging for PR 542 (basic generation smoke).

Decision register (what we decided and why):
- D1: Fast-track PR 542 (runtime connection pooling change) to canary region 2 only. Rationale: Addresses connection tear-down causing cache churn; narrow blast radius. Owner: Marco. Target: 2024-11-06 01:00 UTC. Rollback signal: p95 > 1500ms sustained > 5 minutes or >1% error rate.
- D2: Defer RLE-1991 (model-routing tweaks) to next maintenance window — requires more integration testing with dedicated. Owner: Jordan. Target: 2024-11-12. Rationale: dependency on dedicated autoscaler changes.
- D3: Add temporary rate-limit on internal long-seq test harness to avoid skewing canary metrics. Owner: Elena. Implement by 2024-11-05 EOD.

Action items (concrete):
- A1: Marco — coordinate canary push for PR 542, create rollback playbook snippet, and post canary checklist in thread. Due: 2024-11-06 00:30 UTC. (Linked PR: runtime/pull/542)
- A2: QA (Aisha) — run long-seq regression suite against the canary image; capture token-level traces and sample outputs for quality check. Due: during canary window.
- A3: SRE (Ravi) — add temporary Prometheus alert with 5-minute p95 sliding window flagged to release-ops; ensure synthetic spike test runs 10 minutes pre-deploy. Due: 2024-11-05 19:00 UTC.
- A4: Elena — throttle internal test harness and update runbook. Due: 2024-11-05 23:59 UTC.
- A5: Priya — prepare post-canary decision note (pass/fail + next steps) and runbook update. Due: 2024-11-06 06:00 UTC.

Rollout plan (canary -> ramp):
- Canary region: eu-west-2 small pool (2 pods) at 100% for model-runtime image with PR 542. Duration: 2 hours.
- Validation: synthetic test (10 minutes pre), smoke generator (10 requests x 3 models), QA long-seq suite.
- Ramp policy: only if p95 < 700ms and error rate < 0.1% for sustained 30 minutes -> scale to canary pool size 8 and re-evaluate for 1 hour before broader ramp.
- Fallback: immediate rollback to previous image if rollback signals hit or QA flags quality regression.

Risk map (quick):
- Low: minor regressions in non-critical paths, model compatibility regressions (low probability).
- Medium: persistent p95 regressions due to unseen sequence patterns; could increase token cost temporarily.
- High: silent quality regression for top user flows — mitigated by QA checks and sample diffs.

Open blockers & questions:
- Q1: Do we have a quick compare-harness that can diff outputs token-by-token for the top-10 customer prompts? (Jordan to confirm availability; JIRA RLE-2005 tracking).
- Q2: Can dedicated autoscaler changes be decoupled from routing tweak to avoid cascade? (Investigate by 11/08).
- Blocker: Access to eu-west-2 canary GPU pool limited by reserved capacity for Dedicated trials — operations is clearing quota. (Samir following up).

Post-canary notes (added after 11/06 canary window):
- Outcome: Canary stable after 45 minutes; p95 returned to baseline (approx 420ms). No immediate quality regressions observed in sampled outputs.
- Follow-up: PR 542 merged to main at 2024-11-06 03:20 UTC. Short rollforward notes added to runtime CHANGELOG.
- Next steps: schedule broader ramp for 2024-11-07 02:00 UTC if no regressions in broader synthetic load test.

Lessons and heuristics captured (quick):
- Always run long-seq harness 30 minutes prior to any canary push for gen endpoints.
- Add a short-lived internal rate-limit around heavy internal experiments to avoid skewing production canaries.
- When routing changes depend on autoscaler behavior, treat as two separate deploys unless both have explicit integration tests in staging.

Reference links & traces:
- Canaries: eu-west-2/canary-2024-11-06 (SRE console snapshot in linked artifacts).
- PRs: runtime/pull/542 (fix), routing/branch/rle-1987 (deferred).
- Alerts: Prometheus alert id: alert:RLE_CANARY_P95_SPIKE_20241104
- Slack: #release-ops thread rapid-deploy-2024-11-04 (contains post-canary logs and screenshots)

Next meeting / sync
- Quick async check-in on channel at 2024-11-06 09:00 UTC to confirm rollforward schedule.
- Formal weekly release runbook review scheduled 2024-11-07 16:00 UTC (owners: Priya + Marco).

Notes to self / rough TODOs (scratch):
- Add sample failing traces to Confluence page.
- Create one-line rollout SOP for QA to follow when canary declared 'stable'.
- Follow-up ticket: RLE-2002 (post-deploy cost analysis after runtime change)

-- end of notes --

Unresolved: keep this doc as living log; append postmortem if regressions appear. For urgent escalations call release pager and ping #exec-ops if broader customer impact suspected.
